_**User**_

i want to add a new type of notification. currentluy they are set to just send at a given time.

In the new type of notification, we wil only send a notification if the daily amount poppy has been fed is less than some threshold.

So for example, 
At 6 PM, if Poppy has been fed less than 100% of the goal, then send a notification that says how much she's eaten.

These will be called 'feeding reminders'. a user can create their own feeding reminder by saying "if poppy hasn't eaten X% of her daily target by Y time, then display a notification"

Then, when the time to notify comes, we should check if she has been fed enough food, and if not, then display the notification.

2. **Required Changes**:

a) **Data Model Changes**:
- We'll need to extend the `NotificationSchedule` interface to include a new type for conditional feeding reminders
- New fields needed:
  - `type: "time" | "feeding_reminder"`
  - `threshold: number` (percentage of daily goal)
  - The existing fields (id, time, title, body) will still be used

b) **Service Layer Changes**:
- Modify `NotificationService` to handle the new type of notification
- Instead of using Expo's daily trigger, we'll need to use a custom trigger that:
  1. Schedules the check for the specified time
  2. When triggered, checks the current feeding amount from `FeedingContext`
  3. Only sends the notification if the condition is met

c) **UI Changes**:
- Modify `AddReminderModal` to allow users to:
  1. Select between regular time-based reminder or feeding reminder
  2. Input the threshold percentage
  3. Select the time to check

3. **Technical Feasibility**:
Yes, this is definitely possible! Here's why:
- Expo Notifications supports custom trigger logic
- We have access to the feeding data through `FeedingContext`
- The existing notification infrastructure can be extended

1. First, update the data models and interfaces
2. Modify the notification service to support conditional checks
3. Update the UI components to support creating these notifications
4. Add the logic to check feeding amounts at scheduled times
5. Implement dynamic notification message generation based on current feeding amounts

1. **Data Model Updates**:
```typescript
// In notification-schedules.ts
export interface BaseNotificationSchedule {
  id: string;
  time: string; // HH:mm format
  title: string;
  body: string;
}

export interface TimeBasedNotification extends BaseNotificationSchedule {
  type: 'time';
}

export interface FeedingReminderNotification extends BaseNotificationSchedule {
  type: 'feeding_reminder';
  threshold: number; // Percentage of daily target (0-100)
  // We'll use the body field as a template, replacing {amount} and {target} with actual values
}

export type NotificationSchedule = TimeBasedNotification | FeedingReminderNotification;
```

2. **NotificationService Updates**:
```typescript
// New method in NotificationService class
async scheduleFeedingReminderNotification(schedule: FeedingReminderNotification) {
  const [hours, minutes] = schedule.time.split(":").map(Number);
  
  // We'll schedule a task that:
  // 1. Runs at the specified time
  // 2. Checks the feeding amount
  // 3. Only sends notification if threshold not met
  
  await Notifications.scheduleNotificationAsync({
    content: {
      title: schedule.title,
      body: schedule.body, // Will be populated at notification time
      data: { 
        id: schedule.id,
        type: 'feeding_reminder',
        threshold: schedule.threshold
      },
    },
    trigger: {
      hour: hours,
      minute: minutes,
      repeats: true,
      type: "daily",
    }
  });
}
```

3. **Notification Handler Updates**:
```typescript
// In NotificationService class
private async handleScheduledNotification(notification: Notifications.Notification) {
  const data = notification.request.content.data;
  
  if (data?.type === 'feeding_reminder') {
    // Get current feeding data
    const feedingContext = useFeeding();
    const { todayData } = feedingContext.state;
    
    if (!todayData) return; // No data available
    
    const percentageFed = (todayData.amountFed / todayData.target) * 100;
    
    // Only send notification if below threshold
    if (percentageFed < data.threshold) {
      const body = notification.request.content.body
        .replace('{amount}', todayData.amountFed.toString())
        .replace('{target}', todayData.target.toString())
        .replace('{percentage}', percentageFed.toFixed(1));
        
      await Notifications.scheduleNotificationAsync({
        content: {
          title: notification.request.content.title,
          body: body,
        },
        trigger: null, // Send immediately
      });
    }
  }
}
```

4. **UI Updates**:
```typescript

}
```

This means we can accurately calculate the percentage fed at any time and make the notification decision based on real data.

_**Assistant**_

No, the notifications won't get deleted when the user closes the app. Here's why:

1. The notifications are scheduled using Expo's `scheduleNotificationAsync` with a `DailyTriggerInput` trigger type, which persists even when the app is closed
2. The schedules are registered with the device's notification system through Expo, which maintains them independently of the app's state
3. The `NotificationService` initializes and reschedules all notifications when the app starts up (in `_layout.tsx`), ensuring they're always properly set up

The only time notifications would be cleared is if:
1. The app is uninstalled
2. The user explicitly cancels them
3. We call `cancelAllScheduledNotifications()`
4. The user revokes notification permissions

Looking at `schedule.tsx`, we're currently just loading `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS` in the `useEffect`, which means every time the component mounts, it will reset the displayed schedules to the defaults, discarding any custom notifications the user has created.

While the actual notifications might still be scheduled with the system (through Expo's notification system), the UI won't show them because we're not persisting and retrieving the user's custom schedules anywhere.

To fix this, we need to:
1. Store the user's schedules (both default and custom) in persistent storage (like AsyncStorage)
2. Load from that storage instead of always using `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS`
3. Only use `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS` as a fallback when there's no saved data

```diff
+ import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
+ import { NotificationSchedule, DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS } from "./notification-schedules";
+ 
+ const STORAGE_KEY = "poppy_tracker_notification_schedules";
+ 
+ export class NotificationStorageService {
+   private static instance: NotificationStorageService;
+ 
+   private constructor() {}
+ 
+   static getInstance(): NotificationStorageService {
+     if (!NotificationStorageService.instance) {
+       NotificationStorageService.instance = new NotificationStorageService();
+     }
+     return NotificationStorageService.instance;
+   }
+ 
+   async getSchedules(): Promise<NotificationSchedule[]> {
+     try {
+       const storedSchedules = await AsyncStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
+       if (!storedSchedules) {
+         // If no schedules are stored, save and return defaults
+         await this.saveSchedules(DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS);
+         return DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS;
+       }
+       return JSON.parse(storedSchedules);
+     } catch (error) {
+       console.error("Failed to load notification schedules:", error);
+       return DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS;
+     }
+   }
+ 
+   async saveSchedules(schedules: NotificationSchedule[]): Promise<void> {
+     try {
+       await AsyncStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(schedules));
+     } catch (error) {
+       console.error("Failed to save notification schedules:", error);
+       throw error;
+     }
+   }
+ 
+   async resetToDefaults(): Promise<NotificationSchedule[]> {
+     try {
+       await this.saveSchedules(DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS);
+       return DEFAULT_NOTIFICATIONS;
+     } catch (error) {
+       console.error("Failed to reset notification schedules:", error);
+       throw error;
+     }
+   }
+ }
```
